passages.text: Then three years passed without war between Aram and Israel.
passages.sermon:
Aram was a nation.
Israel was a nation.
Three years passed.
There was no war between Aram and Israel during those three years.
passages.original: וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים אֵ֚ין מִלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אֲרָ֖ם וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: However, in the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to visit the king of Israel, who said to his servants, “Do you not know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, but we have failed to take it from the hand of the king of Aram?”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
In the third year, Jehoshaphat went down to visit the king of Israel.
The king of Israel spoke to his servants.
He said, “Do you know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us?”
He said, “We have not taken Ramoth-gilead from the king of Aram.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑ית וַיֵּ֛רֶד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֔יו הַיְדַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־ לָ֖נוּ רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ מַחְשִׁ֔ים מִקַּ֣חַת אֹתָ֔הּ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָֽם׃

passages.text: So he asked Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to fight against Ramoth-gilead?” Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel, “I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.
He asked Jehoshaphat a question.
He said, “Will you go with me to fight at Ramoth-gilead?”
Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat said, “I am like you.”
“My people are like your people.”
“My horses are like your horses.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֛י לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּמ֧וֹנִי כָמ֛וֹךָ כְּעַמִּ֥י כְעַמֶּ֖ךָ כְּסוּסַ֥י כְּסוּסֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for the word of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
The king of Israel was with him.
Jehoshaphat spoke to the king of Israel.
He said, “Please ask for the word of the LORD today.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דְּרָשׁ־ נָ֥א כַיּ֖וֹם אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, about four hundred men, and asked them, “Should I go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should I refrain?” “Go up,” they replied, “and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel gathered the prophets.
He brought together about four hundred men.
He spoke to the prophets.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Should I go to war against Ramoth-gilead?”
He also asked, “Or should I not go?”
The prophets answered him.
They said, “Go up.”
They said, “The Lord will give Ramoth-gilead into the king’s hand.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ץ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֶֽת־ הַנְּבִיאִים֮ כְּאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת אִישׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם הַאֵלֵ֞ךְ עַל־ רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם־ אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ עֲלֵ֔ה וְיִתֵּ֥ן אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
He spoke to the king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat asked a question.
He said, “Is there another prophet of the LORD here?”
He wanted to ask the LORD for guidance through that prophet.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֥ה נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה ע֑וֹד וְנִדְרְשָׁ֖ה מֵאוֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The king of Israel answered, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” “The king should not say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.
He said, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD for us.”
He said, “I hate him.”
He said, “He never prophesies anything good about me.”
He said, “He only prophesies bad things.”
He said, “His name is Micaiah son of Imlah.”
Jehoshaphat replied to the king.
Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say that.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל׀ אֶֽל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט ע֣וֹד אִישׁ־ אֶחָ֡ד לִדְרֹשׁ֩ אֶת־ יְהוָ֨ה מֵאֹת֜וֹ וַאֲנִ֣י שְׂנֵאתִ֗יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ יִתְנַבֵּ֨א עָלַ֥י טוֹב֙ כִּ֣י אִם־ רָ֔ע מִיכָ֖יְהוּ בֶּן־ יִמְלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט אַל־ יֹאמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel sat on his throne.
He wore royal clothes.
He called for one of his officials.
He spoke to the official.
He said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־ סָרִ֖יס אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַהֲרָ֖ה מִיכָ֥יְהוּ בֶן־ יִמְלָֽה׃

passages.text: Dressed in royal attire, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel was present.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Both kings were sitting on their thrones.
They wore royal clothes.
They sat at the threshing floor.
This place was by the entrance of the gate of Samaria.
All the prophets stood before them.
All the prophets were prophesying.
passages.original: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֡ה יֹשְׁבִים֩ אִ֨ישׁ עַל־ כִּסְא֜וֹ מְלֻבָּשִׁ֤ים בְּגָדִים֙ בְּגֹ֔רֶן פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְכָ֨ל־ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made for himself iron horns and declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are finished off.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was the son of Chenaanah.
He made iron horns for himself.
He spoke to the people.
He said, “This is what the LORD says.”
He said, “With these iron horns, you will gore the Arameans.”
He said, “You will do this until the Arameans are finished off.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥ה בֶֽן־ כְּנַעֲנָ֖ה קַרְנֵ֣י בַרְזֶ֑ל וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵ֛לֶּה תְּנַגַּ֥ח אֶת־ אֲרָ֖ם עַד־ כַּלֹּתָֽם׃

passages.text: And all the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
passages.sermon:
All the prophets spoke together.
They all gave the same message.
They said, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead.
You will succeed.
The LORD will give the city into the king’s hand.”
passages.original: וְכָל־ הַנְּבִאִ֔ים נִבְּאִ֥ים כֵּ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲלֵ֞ה רָמֹ֤ת גִּלְעָד֙ וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah instructed him, “Behold now, with one accord the words of the prophets are favorable to the king. So please let your words be like theirs, and speak favorably.”
passages.sermon:
A messenger went to find Micaiah.
This messenger spoke to Micaiah.
He said, “All the prophets speak together with one voice.
They speak good things to the king.
Let your words be like the words of one of them.
Speak good things.”
passages.original: וְהַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ אֲשֶׁר־ הָלַ֣ךְ׀ לִקְרֹ֣א מִיכָ֗יְהוּ דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּה־ נָ֞א דִּבְרֵ֧י הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים פֶּֽה־ אֶחָ֥ד ט֖וֹב אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ יְהִֽי־ נָ֣א דִבְרֶיךָ כִּדְבַ֛ר אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶ֖ם וְדִבַּ֥רְתָּ טּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: But Micaiah said, “As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me.”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to the messenger.
Micaiah said, “The LORD lives.”
Micaiah said, “I will speak only what the LORD tells me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִיכָ֑יְהוּ חַי־ יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֠י אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: When Micaiah arrived, the king asked him, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up and triumph,” Micaiah replied, “for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
The king of Israel called Micaiah to him.
The king spoke to Micaiah.
The king asked, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead?”
The king also asked, “Or should we hold back and not go?”
Micaiah answered the king.
Micaiah said, “Go up and succeed.”
Micaiah said, “The LORD will give Ramoth-gilead into the hand of the king.”
passages.original: וַיָּבוֹא֮ אֶל־ הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֵלָ֗יו מִיכָ֙יְהוּ֙ הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל־ רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם־ נֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ עֲלֵ֣ה וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: But the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Micaiah.
The king said, “How many times must I make you swear?”
The king wanted Micaiah to promise something.
The king said, “You must not speak to me anything except the truth.”
The king said, “You must speak only in the name of the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד־ כַּמֶּ֥ה פְעָמִ֖ים אֲנִ֣י מַשְׁבִּעֶ֑ךָ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ תְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י רַק־ אֱמֶ֖ת בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So Micaiah declared: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet.
Micaiah spoke to the king.
Micaiah said, “I saw all Israel.”
The people of Israel were scattered on the hills.
They were like sheep without a shepherd.
The LORD spoke.
The LORD said, “These people have no master.”
The LORD said, “Let each one return home in peace.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְפֹצִ֣ים אֶל־ הֶהָרִ֔ים כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־ לָהֶ֖ם רֹעֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לֹֽא־ אֲדֹנִ֣ים לָאֵ֔לֶּה יָשׁ֥וּבוּ אִישׁ־ לְבֵית֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good for me, but only bad?”
passages.sermon: The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.\r\nHe said, “Did I not tell you this prophet never prophesies good for me?\r\nHe only prophesies bad for me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט הֲלוֹא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֽוֹא־ יִתְנַבֵּ֥א עָלַ֛י ט֖וֹב כִּ֥י אִם־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: Micaiah continued, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left.
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to the people.
Micaiah said, "Listen to the word of the LORD."
Micaiah saw a vision.
Micaiah saw the LORD.
The LORD was sitting on His throne.
All the host of heaven stood near the LORD.
Some stood on the LORD’s right side.
Some stood on the LORD’s left side.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָכֵ֖ן שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֑ה רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב עַל־ כִּסְא֔וֹ וְכָל־ צְבָ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And the LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ And one suggested this, and another that.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD asked a question.
Ahab was the king of Israel.
The LORD said, “Who will entice Ahab?”
The LORD wanted Ahab to go up to Ramoth-gilead.
The LORD wanted Ahab to fall there.
Different ones answered the LORD.
One suggested one way.
Another suggested a different way.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה מִ֤י יְפַתֶּה֙ אֶת־ אַחְאָ֔ב וְיַ֕עַל וְיִפֹּ֖ל בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר זֶה֙ בְּכֹ֔ה וְזֶ֥ה אֹמֵ֖ר בְּכֹֽה׃

passages.text: Then a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD, and said, ‘I will entice him.’ ‘By what means?’ asked the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A spirit came forward.
The spirit stood before the LORD.
The spirit said, “I will entice him.”
The LORD asked the spirit, “By what means?”
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָר֗וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲנִ֣י אֲפַתֶּ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו בַּמָּֽה׃

passages.text: And he replied, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ ‘You will surely entice him and prevail,’ said the LORD. ‘Go and do it.’
passages.sermon:
A spirit stood before the LORD.
The spirit spoke to the LORD.
The spirit said, “I will go out.”
The spirit said, “I will be a lying spirit.”
The spirit said, “I will be in the mouths of all Ahab’s prophets.”
The LORD answered the spirit.
The LORD said, “You will entice Ahab.”
The LORD said, “You will succeed.”
The LORD said, “Go.”
The LORD said, “Do this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵצֵא֙ וְהָיִ֙יתִי֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל־ נְבִיאָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּפַתֶּה֙ וְגַם־ תּוּכָ֔ל צֵ֖א וַעֲשֵׂה־ כֵֽן׃

passages.text: So you see, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, and the LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has power over spirits.
The LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all your prophets.
These prophets speak lies because of the LORD’s action.
The LORD has declared disaster against you.
You will face harm because the LORD has spoken it.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל־ נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah went up, struck Micaiah in the face, and demanded, “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He departed from me to speak with you?”
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was the son of Chenaanah.
He went up to Micaiah.
Zedekiah struck Micaiah on the face.
Zedekiah demanded an answer.
He said, “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He left me to speak with you?”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶֽן־ כְּנַעֲנָ֔ה וַיַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת־ מִיכָ֖יְהוּ עַל־ הַלֶּ֑חִי וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵי־ זֶ֨ה עָבַ֧ר רֽוּחַ־ יְהוָ֛ה מֵאִתִּ֖י לְדַבֵּ֥ר אוֹתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Micaiah replied, “You will soon see, on that day when you go and hide in an inner room.”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to Zedekiah.
Micaiah said, “You will see the truth soon.”
On that day, you will go into an inner room.
You will hide there.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ הִנְּךָ֥ רֹאֶ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֛א חֶ֥דֶר בְּחֶ֖דֶר לְהֵחָבֵֽה׃

passages.text: And the king of Israel declared, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king’s son, and tell them that this is what the king says: ‘Put this man in prison and feed him only bread and water until I return safely.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke.
He gave a command about Micaiah.
He said, “Take Micaiah.”
“Return him to Amon.”
Amon was the governor of the city.
Return him also to Joash.
Joash was the king’s son.
Tell them what the king says.
The king says, ‘Put this man in prison.’
Feed him only bread and water.
Do this until I return safely.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קַ֚ח אֶת־ מִיכָ֔יְהוּ וַהֲשִׁיבֵ֖הוּ אֶל־ אָמֹ֣ן שַׂר־ הָעִ֑יר וְאֶל־ יוֹאָ֖שׁ בֶּן־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שִׂ֥ימוּ אֶת־ זֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית הַכֶּ֑לֶא וְהַאֲכִילֻ֨הוּ לֶ֤חֶם לַ֙חַץ֙ וּמַ֣יִם לַ֔חַץ עַ֖ד בֹּאִ֥י בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: But Micaiah replied, “If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Take heed, all you people!”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to the king of Israel.
Micaiah said, “If you return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.”
Micaiah then spoke to everyone present.
Micaiah said, “Listen, all you people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ אִם־ שׁ֤וֹב תָּשׁוּב֙ בְּשָׁל֔וֹם לֹֽא־ דִבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְע֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel was Ahab.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Ahab and Jehoshaphat went together.
They went up to Ramoth-gilead.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַל מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.
The king of Israel said, "I will disguise myself and go into battle."
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "You wear your royal robes."
The king of Israel disguised himself.
The king of Israel went into battle.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט הִתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ וָבֹ֣א בַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לְבַ֣שׁ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּב֖וֹא בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Now the king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, “Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram gave an order.
He spoke to his thirty-two chariot commanders.
He said, “Do not fight with anyone else.
Do not fight with anyone small.
Do not fight with anyone great.
Fight only with the king of Israel.”
passages.original: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֡ם צִוָּ֣ה אֶת־ שָׂרֵי֩ הָרֶ֨כֶב אֲשֶׁר־ ל֜וֹ שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֚א תִּלָּ֣חֲמ֔וּ אֶת־ קָטֹ֖ן וְאֶת־ גָּד֑וֹל כִּ֛י אִֽם־ אֶת־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “Surely this is the king of Israel!” So they turned to fight against him, but Jehoshaphat cried out.
passages.sermon:
The chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “This is certainly the king of Israel.”
They turned toward Jehoshaphat.
They prepared to fight against him.
Jehoshaphat cried out.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כִּרְאוֹת֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֜כֶב אֶת־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וְהֵ֤מָּה אָֽמְרוּ֙ אַ֣ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיָּסֻ֥רוּ עָלָ֖יו לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם וַיִּזְעַ֖ק יְהוֹשָׁפָֽט׃

passages.text: And when the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
passages.sermon:
The chariot commanders served the king of Aram.
They looked at Jehoshaphat.
They realized he was not the king of Israel.
They stopped chasing him.
They turned away from him.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְאוֹת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב כִּֽי־ לֹא־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ה֑וּא וַיָּשׁ֖וּבוּ מֵאַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: However, a certain man drew his bow without taking special aim, and he struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So the king said to his charioteer, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am badly wounded!”
passages.sermon:
A certain man was in the battle.
He drew his bow.
He did not take special aim.
He shot an arrow.
The arrow struck the king of Israel.
It hit him between the joints of his armor.
The king of Israel was wounded.
He spoke to his charioteer.
He said, “Turn around.
Take me out of the battle.
I am badly wounded.”
passages.original: וְאִ֗ישׁ מָשַׁ֤ךְ בַּקֶּ֙שֶׁת֙ לְתֻמּ֔וֹ וַיַּכֶּה֙ אֶת־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בֵּ֥ין הַדְּבָקִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַשִּׁרְיָ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְרַכָּב֗וֹ הֲפֹ֥ךְ יָדְךָ֛ וְהוֹצִיאֵ֥נִי מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵֽיתִי׃

passages.text: The battle raged throughout that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans. And the blood from his wound ran out onto the floor of the chariot, and that evening he died.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel fought in a battle against the Arameans.
The battle continued all day.
The king stayed propped up in his chariot.
He faced the Aramean army.
Blood from the king’s wound flowed onto the floor of his chariot.
That evening, the king died.
passages.original: וַתַּעֲלֶ֤ה הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הָיָ֧ה מָעֳמָ֛ד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֖ה נֹ֣כַח אֲרָ֑ם וַיָּ֣מָת בָּעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּ֥צֶק דַּֽם־ הַמַּכָּ֖ה אֶל־ חֵ֥יק הָרָֽכֶב׃

passages.text: As the sun was setting, the cry rang out in the army: “Every man to his own city, and every man to his own land!”
passages.sermon:
The sun began to set.
A loud cry went out through the army.
The cry said, “Every man must return to his own city.”
The cry also said, “Every man must return to his own land.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר הָרִנָּה֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כְּבֹ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־ עִיר֖וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־ אַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So the king died and was brought to Samaria, where they buried him.
passages.sermon: King Ahab died.\r\nPeople brought King Ahab to Samaria.\r\nThey buried King Ahab in Samaria.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣מָת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּב֖וֹא שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: And the chariot was washed at the pool of Samaria where the prostitutes bathed, and the dogs licked up Ahab’s blood, according to the word that the LORD had spoken.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
People brought his chariot to the pool of Samaria.
They washed the chariot at the pool.
Prostitutes bathed at this pool.
Dogs came to the pool.
The dogs licked up Ahab’s blood at the pool.
The LORD had spoken this would happen.
This happened just as the LORD said.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁטֹ֨ף אֶת־ הָרֶ֜כֶב עַ֣ל׀ בְּרֵכַ֣ת שֹׁמְר֗וֹן וַיָּלֹ֤קּוּ הַכְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־ דָּמ֔וֹ וְהַזֹּנ֖וֹת רָחָ֑צוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Ahab, along with all his accomplishments and the ivory palace and all the cities he built, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
passages.sermon:
Ahab was king of Israel.
Ahab did many things.
Ahab built an ivory palace.
Ahab built many cities.
Writers recorded the rest of Ahab’s deeds.
They wrote these things in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י אַחְאָ֜ב וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה וּבֵ֤ית הַשֵּׁן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה וְכָל־ הֶעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Ahab rested with his fathers, and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was king of Israel.
Ahab died.
Ahab joined his ancestors in death.
Ahaziah was Ahab’s son.
Ahaziah became king after Ahab.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אַחְאָ֖ב עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: In the fourth year of Ahab’s reign over Israel, Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the son of Asa.
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ahab had reigned for four years.
In the fourth year of Ahab’s reign, Jehoshaphat became king.
Jehoshaphat became king over Judah.
passages.original: וִיהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ בֶּן־ אָסָ֔א מָלַ֖ךְ עַל־ יְהוּדָ֑ה בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֔ע לְאַחְאָ֖ב מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat became king when he was thirty-five years old.
He ruled in Jerusalem.
He reigned for twenty-five years.
His mother was Azubah.
Azubah was the daughter of Shilhi.
passages.original: יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט בֶּן־ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ עֲזוּבָ֖ה בַּת־ שִׁלְחִֽי׃

passages.text: And Jehoshaphat walked in all the ways of his father Asa; he did not turn away from them, but did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. The high places, however, were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat was the son of Asa.
Jehoshaphat followed all the ways of his father Asa.
Jehoshaphat did not turn away from Asa’s ways.
Jehoshaphat did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
Jehoshaphat did not remove the high places.
The people still sacrificed on the high places.
The people still burned incense on the high places.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּכָל־ דֶּ֛רֶךְ אָסָ֥א אָבִ֖יו לֹא־ סָ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ אַ֥ךְ הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹֽא־ סָ֑רוּ ע֥וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.
passages.sermon: Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.\r\nHe made peace with the king of Israel.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ם יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט עִם־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, along with the might he exercised and how he waged war, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
He did many other things.
He showed great strength.
He fought in battles.
The Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah records these things.
You can read about his other acts there.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט וּגְבוּרָת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נִלְחָ֑ם הֲלֹֽא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: He banished from the land the male shrine prostitutes who remained from the days of his father Asa.
passages.sermon: Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.\r\nSome male shrine prostitutes remained in the land from the days of his father Asa.\r\nJehoshaphat banished these male shrine prostitutes from the land.
passages.original: וְיֶ֙תֶר֙ הַקָּדֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאַ֔ר בִּימֵ֖י אָסָ֣א אָבִ֑יו בִּעֵ֖ר מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And there was no king in Edom; a deputy served as king.
passages.sermon: Edom had no king.\r\nA deputy ruled in place of a king.
passages.original: וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֵ֛ין בֶּאֱד֖וֹם נִצָּ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they never set sail, because they were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish.
He wanted the ships to go to Ophir.
He wanted the ships to bring back gold.
The ships never set sail.
The ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
passages.original: יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט עָשָׂר אֳנִיּ֨וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֜ישׁ לָלֶ֧כֶת אוֹפִ֛ירָה לַזָּהָ֖ב וְלֹ֣א הָלָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־ נִשְׁבְּרָה אֳנִיּ֖וֹת בְּעֶצְי֥וֹן גָּֽבֶר׃

passages.text: At that time Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants sail with your servants,” but Jehoshaphat refused.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah was the son of Ahab.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
At that time, Ahaziah spoke to Jehoshaphat.
Ahaziah said, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships.”
Jehoshaphat refused.
passages.original: אָ֠ז אָמַ֞ר אֲחַזְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־ אַחְאָב֙ אֶל־ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט יֵלְכ֧וּ עֲבָדַ֛י עִם־ עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בָּאֳנִיּ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה יְהוֹשָׁפָֽט׃

passages.text: And Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of his father David. And his son Jehoram reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat died.
Jehoshaphat joined his ancestors in death.
People buried Jehoshaphat with his ancestors.
They buried him in the city of David.
David was Jehoshaphat’s ancestor.
Jehoram was Jehoshaphat’s son.
Jehoram became king after Jehoshaphat.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵר֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ס

passages.text: In the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat’s reign over Judah, Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria two years.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah was the son of Ahab.
Ahaziah became king of Israel.
He began to reign in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Ahaziah ruled in Samaria.
He reigned over Israel for two years.
passages.original: אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַ֣ע עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנָתָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the ways of his father and mother and of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah was king of Israel.
Ahaziah did evil in the sight of the LORD.
Ahaziah followed the ways of his father Ahab.
Ahaziah followed the ways of his mother Jezebel.
Ahaziah followed the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Jeroboam son of Nebat caused Israel to sin.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ אָבִיו֙ וּבְדֶ֣רֶךְ אִמּ֔וֹ וּבְדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Ahaziah served and worshiped Baal, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah was king of Israel.
He was the son of Ahab.
Ahaziah served Baal.
He worshiped Baal.
He made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.
He did these things just as his father had done.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־ הַבַּ֔עַל וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה ל֑וֹ וַיַּכְעֵ֗ס אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה אָבִֽיו׃
